purpose: Primary Fair Work Commission platform case ledger preserving substitute earnings during deactivation, reactivation, and a lost-pay order without treating substitute work or the order as freely chosen alternatives, payment receipt, or durable recovery.

events.geography: Australia; Fair Work Commission matter UDE2025/141, Mansoor v Rasier Pacific
events.date_precision: deactivation date; merits decision and PR792727 order record substitute earnings and later reactivation/payment obligations
events.denominator: One publicly identified adjudicated platform-worker case; no population denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from the primary Fair Work Commission merits decision, reactivation/lost-pay order, and bounded public follow-up recheck
events.missingness: Whether substitute work was equivalent or freely chosen, search effort, expenses, net earnings, payment receipt, actual Uber access, recurrence, household outcome, trust, and exit are not retained
events.exposure: Uber deactivated the worker after a customer complaint and related process; the Commission found the allegations were not proven and the process deficient
events.alternatives_before_action: The worker earned $9,000 from Baysec Group and had an estimated $1,760 increase in Didi earnings during the deactivation period; the public record does not establish the full alternative set, reachability, equivalence, or voluntariness
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Substitute earnings were visible during the interruption and were deducted in calculating a $6,073.23 gross lost-earnings order; expenses, hours, conditions, and residual loss are not observed
events.choice_or_response: The worker pursued the statutory unfair-deactivation route and substitute platform/work activity; the record does not establish whether the alternative work was chosen freely or under constraint
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Uber/Rasier controlled account access and reactivation; the worker controlled the legal challenge and substitute-work response; the Commission controlled adjudication and remedy
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: The Commission ordered reactivation on prior terms and PR792727 required $6,073.23 gross less tax for lost earnings within 14 days
events.remedy_receipt: Payment receipt and actual Uber reactivation are not observed
events.durability_followup: Substitute work is observed, but continued platform work, recurrence, trust, and exit are unknown
events.immediate_outcome: A same-case substitute-earnings surface is linked to a formal reactivation and lost-pay order; payment receipt and practical restoration are not observed
events.protected_outcome: The worker retained some income through Baysec and Didi during the interruption and received a formal route to reactivation and lost-pay recovery
events.sacrificed_outcome: Primary Uber access and associated earnings were interrupted; the record does not measure waiting, search cost, expenses, household substitution, or durable income loss
events.cost_risk_transfer: The worker carried the burden of substitute work and legal pursuit while the platform retained control over access and the ordered remedy remained subject to execution
events.later_outcome: Substitute work and formal restoration are observed, but payment receipt, actual Uber reactivation, continued work, recurrence, household recovery, trust, switching, non-use, and exit remain unknown
events.meaning_and_attribution: The merits route records a challenge to the platform's process, but no standardized trust, fairness, blame, identity, or later-action measure is retained
events.public_or_collective_response: The worker used an individual statutory adjudication route; no later collective or political action is reported
events.counterexample: Substitute earnings can reduce a formal lost-pay award without proving equivalent work, free choice, payment receipt, restored access, or durable recovery
events.source_and_uncertainty: Fair Work Commission [2025] FWC 3111 and PR792727; https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/decisionssigned/pdf/2025fwc3111.pdf and https://www.fwc.gov.au/documents/awardsandorders/pdf/pr792727.pdf; public follow-up recheck found no later receipt or durable-access record

arrows.evidence: The merits decision records $9,000 in Baysec earnings and an estimated $1,760 increase in Didi earnings after deactivation
arrows.counterexample: Observed substitute earnings do not establish a freely chosen, equivalent, reachable, or net-positive alternative
arrows.remaining_gap: Offer set, search effort, hours, expenses, conditions, eligibility, and net household effect

arrows.evidence: The Commission deducted substitute earnings when calculating the $6,073.23 gross lost-earnings order
arrows.counterexample: A legal deduction is not a welfare-equivalent measure or proof that substitute work restored access
arrows.remaining_gap: Actual hours, expenses, equivalence, residual loss, and household incidence

arrows.evidence: The Commission found the process deficient, ordered reactivation on prior terms, and PR792727 set a $6,073.23 gross payment obligation with a deadline
arrows.counterexample: An order and deadline do not establish actual access restoration or payment receipt
arrows.remaining_gap: Platform implementation, payment execution, receipt, and net recovery

arrows.to: durable access, trust, switching, or exit
arrows.evidence: The public follow-up found no later receipt, actual access, continued Uber work, switching, non-use, household recovery, recurrence, or exit record
arrows.counterexample: Alternative work and a formal order can coexist with continued dependence, unresolved loss, or unobserved exit
arrows.remaining_gap: Receipt, actual access, job/platform duration, recurrence, household recovery, trust, switching, non-use, and exit

arrows.evidence: The record orders an individual remedy but reports no platform-wide process correction, recurrence monitoring, or anti-retaliation follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Individual reactivation and compensation can coexist with unchanged platform governance
arrows.remaining_gap: Process correction, recurrence, worker voice, monitoring, and comparable-worker outcomes

boundary: This ledger adds a same-case platform episode with observed substitute earnings and formal restoration/lost-pay orders. It does not establish that the alternative was free or equivalent, that the order was paid, that access was restored in practice, or that recovery, trust, switching, or exit followed.
storage_boundary: No worker file, direct identifier beyond the public case reference, payment instrument, or bulk archive is retained; only bounded primary decision/order fields, dates, substitute earnings, remedy stages, uncertainty, and open downstream arrows are represented.
